key_insight: A concatenated GKP + Steane all-photonic repeater can extend quantum communication to 1,000 km with 9 km spacing while remaining resource-efficient.
engineering_relevance: The design reduces photon-loss bottlenecks in quantum networks and offers a practical path toward scalable, long-distance photonic quantum repeaters.
method: Use bosonic GKP encoding inside the [[7,1,3]] Steane code to boost loss tolerance.
Add a multi-reflection mirror optical cavity as a free-space photonic memory model.
Construct elementary Bell pairs with two heuristic schemes that trade correlated-error tolerance against GKP-qubit count.
evidence_signal: Simulations including switching-induced imperfections and standard optical losses indicate only a few thousand GKP qubits are needed per repeater station per protocol run.
watch_item: The architecture depends on realistic high-efficiency mirrors, low-loss switching, and accurate preparation of encoded Bell pairs, which may be difficult to realize experimentally.
paper_title: High-Rate and Resource-Efficient All-Photonic Quantum Repeater Architectures with 9 km Repeater Spacing
